subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `cron.minInterval` as the operator-controlled enforcement contract for high-frequency recurring cron jobs?
rationale: This is not just a bug fix: it adds a public config key and changes behavior for configured deployments by rejecting or pacing schedules that were previously valid and silent.

options.title: Accept Opt-In Enforcement
options.body: Proceed with `cron.minInterval` as the shared service-level guardrail after the generated docs map is fixed and current checks are refreshed.

options.title: Keep Advisory-Only Behavior
options.body: Reject or defer this PR if maintainers prefer warnings without schedule rejection or fire-time pacing.

options.title: Defer To Broader Cron Policy
options.body: Pause this PR if cadence limits should be bundled with retention, context-pressure, or session-cleanup policy instead of landing as one config key.

recommendation.title: Accept Opt-In Enforcement
recommendation.body: Proceed with `cron.minInterval` as the shared service-level guardrail after the generated docs map is fixed and current checks are refreshed.

likelyOwner.reason: The live PR is assigned to and requests review from vincentkoc, who also has recent adjacent cron runtime history.
